parent.title: AI-Assisted Code Review in 2026: Landscape, Tools, Evidence, and Limits

siblings.title: Market map: commercial vendors and platforms
siblings.summary: Landscape of 19 commercial vendors across four segments — standalone PR review, platform-bundled, code quality/security, and enterprise-privacy.

siblings.title: Open-source tools, agents, and research ecosystem
siblings.summary: The open-source side of AI code review — review tools, autonomous agents, agent frameworks, and the open-weight code LLMs underneath.

siblings.title: Agentic code review workflows
siblings.summary: How agentic code review differs from single-pass LLM bots, the 2026 tool landscape, and the gap between vendor benchmarks and independent evidence.

siblings.title: Risks, limitations, and adoption barriers
siblings.summary: The accuracy ceiling, live security holes, human-factor friction, and legal exposure that keep AI code review a triage aid rather than a merge gate.

siblings.title: Security-specific review tooling
siblings.summary: SAST, SCA, and secrets scanning tools form the foundation of modern AppSec.

sources.title: SWRBench (arXiv 2509.01494)
sources.claim: 1000 verified PRs; multi-review aggregation boosts F1 by up to 43.67%

sources.title: SWRBench full paper (arXiv 2509.01494v1)
sources.claim: Best configuration F1 19.38% (PR-Review + Gemini-2.5-Pro); 500 Change-PRs, 500 Clean-PRs, 12 Python projects

sources.title: CRScore (NAACL 2025)
sources.claim: Reference-free metric across conciseness/comprehensiveness/relevance; 2.9k human-annotated scores

sources.title: CRScore paper (arXiv 2409.19801v2)
sources.claim: Spearman 0.5431 vs humans; valid review can score BLEU 0.0458

sources.title: Microsoft CodeReviewer (arXiv 2203.09095)
sources.claim: 7.9M PRs, 9 languages; BLEU stays <10

sources.title: CodeReviewQA (arXiv 2503.16167)
sources.claim: 900 MCQA cases: recognition, localization, solution

sources.title: 2026 benchmark survey (arXiv 2602.13377v1)
sources.claim: 99 papers 2015-2025; benchmarks and metrics remain immature

sources.title: CodeReviewer data quality (arXiv 2502.02757)
sources.claim: Only 64% of training comments valid; BLEU +7.5-13% with clean data

sources.title: AIDev in-the-wild study (arXiv 2604.03196v1)
sources.claim: 12 of 13 agents <60% signal; Copilot 19.79%; CRA-only PRs merge at 45.20% vs 68.37% human

sources.title: CodeFuse-CR-Bench (arXiv 2509.14856)
sources.claim: Comprehensiveness-aware benchmark for end-to-end code review evaluation

sources.title: Greptile Benchmarks
sources.claim: Greptile 82% catch rate; Bugbot 58%, Copilot 54%, CodeRabbit 44%, Graphite 6%; 50 bug-fix PRs

sources.title: CodeRabbit: Martian Benchmark
sources.claim: F1 51.2%, recall 53.5% #1 on Martian Bench (~300k PRs)

sources.title: CodeAnt: Martian Benchmark Results
sources.claim: F1 51.7%, precision 52.2%, recall 51.1%, rank #3 on Martian Bench

sources.title: Cursor: Building BugBot
sources.claim: Resolution rate rose from 52% to 70%+; BugBench curated real diffs

sources.title: Qodo: How we built a benchmark
sources.claim: 100 PRs, 580 LLM-injected issues, 7 repos; hit = correct description + file/line

sources.title: Qodo 2.0 launch
sources.claim: F1 60.1%, recall 56.7% on Qodo's own benchmark

sources.title: Bito: Benchmarking AI Code Review
sources.claim: Bito 69.5%, CodeRabbit 65.8%; 65-issue truth set, 5 languages

sources.title: Graphite: Diamond launch
sources.claim: $52M Series B; Diamond optimized for low FP; acquired by Cursor Dec 2025

sources.title: Korbit: Precision matters most
sources.claim: Precision-first positioning; suppress low-value comments

sources.title: DeepSource: AI Code Review Benchmarks
sources.claim: Every vendor benchmarks itself and wins; datasets incomparable

sources.title: Propel Benchmarks
sources.claim: Propel 64%, Cursor BugBot 49%, Greptile 45% on Propel's board

sources.title: Graphite: AI Code Review False Positives
sources.claim: Typical FPR 5-15%; well-tuned tools 5-8%

sources.title: Augment Code: Recall vs Precision
sources.claim: 46% distrust AI accuracy; 66% cite 'almost right but not quite'

sources.title: HN: AI Code Reviewers discussion
sources.claim: Only small fraction of AI review comments are useful; junior engineers sent into rabbit holes

sources.title: CodeAnt: False Positives
sources.claim: Noisy reviewer erodes trust through 3-stage cycle ending in dismiss-all

sources.title: Microsoft Research: Useful Code Reviews
sources.claim: Useful = triggers nearby code change; ~1/3 of 1.5M comments non-useful

sources.title: 'Hold On!' usefulness study (arXiv 2501.06738)
sources.claim: >1 in 3 comments lack utility; predicts usefulness via Code/Text/Voice/Jargon features

sources.title: Snorkel AI: Data Quality and Rubrics
sources.claim: Behavioral level-definitions over vague labels; BWS more reliable than Likert

sources.title: Maxim: Building a Golden Dataset
sources.claim: Promote silver synthetic to gold via evaluator agreement; pilot annotator calibration

sources.title: Rubric-based Evals: LLM-as-Judge
sources.claim: Rubrics bridge human policy language and machine-checkable rewards; IRT to retire ambiguous criteria

sources.title: MT-Bench/Chatbot Arena (arXiv 2306.05685)
sources.claim: GPT-4 judges >80% agreement with humans; position/verbosity/self-enhancement biases

sources.title: Self-preference bias (arXiv 2410.21819)
sources.claim: Self-preference = perplexity/familiarity effect; LLMs reward low-perplexity regardless of author

sources.title: LLM-as-Judge Bias & Reliability
sources.claim: Order swap shifts accuracy >10%; expert-domain agreement 60-68%

sources.title: Debiasing strategies (arXiv 2604.23178)
sources.claim: +7.2 to +11.2pp gains from debiasing; optimal strategy is model-dependent

sources.title: Adaline: LLM-as-Judge Reliability
sources.claim: Use cross-provider judge; reference-guided grading; human spot-check calibration

sources.title: SWE-bench Verified Leaderboard
sources.claim: June 2026: Claude Mythos Preview 93.9%, Opus 4.8 88.6%; 97 models

sources.title: SWE-bench Verified dataset
sources.claim: 500 human-validated issues; 68.3% of original filtered out

sources.title: CodeAnt: SWE-bench Scores
sources.claim: 80%+ on Verified → 46-57% on Pro; contamination-resistant private codebases

sources.title: LiveCodeBench Leaderboard
sources.claim: Contamination-free by construction; date-stamped problems from LeetCode/AtCoder/CodeForces

sources.title: BigCodeBench
sources.claim: 1,140 practical tasks; calibrated Pass@1

sources.title: RepoBench (arXiv 2306.03091)
sources.claim: Repo-level completion: Retrieval, Completion, Pipeline tasks for Python/Java

sources.title: Contamination study (arXiv 2506.12286v4)
sources.claim: 76% buggy-file ID from issue text alone; 11.7-31.6% verbatim memorization

sources.title: SWE-rebench: decontaminated tests
sources.claim: 32.67% of o3 successes leaked from issue text; 59.4% of failures were test-harness flaws

sources.title: Reproducibility of LLM papers (arXiv 2510.25506)
sources.claim: 85 ICSE/ASE 2024 papers: 18 shared artifacts, 5 executable, 0 fully reproduced

sources.title: CR-Bench SNR (arXiv 2603.11078v1)
sources.claim: Signal-to-noise ratio as proxy for developer trust; high recall + excess output → fatigue

sources.title: Ground truth noise (arXiv 2604.24525v1)
sources.claim: Human PR comments are noisy artifacts; clarification questions and style nits corrupt labels

sources.title: SE benchmark construct validity (arXiv 2503.05860v2)
sources.claim: Nearly every SE benchmark has at least one construct-validity weakness

sources.title: Best-Worst Scaling (arXiv 1712.01765)
sources.claim: BWS ρ=0.98 vs rating scale ρ=0.95 (p<.001); matches reliability with 3N vs 10N annotations

sources.title: BWS for first impressions (Cognitive Research 2019)
sources.claim: BWS improves measurement reliability over rating scales in social-perception data

sources.title: Krippendorff's alpha (arXiv 2603.06865)
sources.claim: Krippendorff α handles missing data, any number of raters, nominal/ordinal/interval; high IAA confirms consistency not construct validity
